beats.text: Ethernet is named after the ether.
beats.note: Luminiferous ether was the 19th century idea of a medium that carried light.

beats.name: Bob Metcalfe
beats.role: Wrote the memo to Xerox PARC management explaining how Ethernet would work. It is dated 22 May.

beats.text: He did not call it coax-net.
beats.note: The first network ran at 2.94 Mbit/s over shared coaxial cable at Xerox PARC.
Metcalfe: coax, twisted pair, radio, optical fibre, power line, whatever you wanted.

beats.context: The reach of the 1983 standard for 10 Mbit/s Ethernet over coaxial cable.

beats.text: He named it for the medium, not the cable.
